item.title: Building a Custom Mythic Agent from Scratch (in Python)
item.description: This is the continuation of this article ## Introduction Now that we have a working Mythic setup, we’re able to deep diver into C2 architecture and start integrating our own tools and techniques to the base platform. The goal is simple: Understand how an agent really works internally Build my own minimal implant Extend it with a custom command tied to a real-world privilege escalation exploit Integrate everything cleanly into Mythic’s tasking system Understanding the Agent Model To get started, we have example containers available to help us understand the file structures.

item.title: Getting Started with Mythic C2: Installation, Configuration, and First Callback
item.description: This is Part 1 of a series on Mythic C2. As an offensive cybersecurity professional, learning about C2 frameworks feels essential. I spent some time researching different options and narrowed it down to two popular open source projects: Mythic and Sliver. Both are widely used in red team and adversary emulation work, but I chose Mythic because of its modular architecture and flexibility. Mythic separates agents and communication profiles into individual components that can be dynamically installed and extended, which felt like a good platform for learning and experimentation.
